Early backer of Cohere, Waabi and Xanadu.

strategy.thesis: Thesis-driven growth-equity firm investing in high-growth B2B software companies leveraging applied AI; operates an in-house AI Lab of 20+ ML engineers and data scientists that works with portfolio companies on production AI deployment.

summary.en: Toronto-based growth-equity firm founded in 2008, focused on high-growth B2B software companies applying AI. Manages roughly US$5.7 billion AUM (Sept 2025), typically writing US$20M-75M checks at Series B and later. Backed Shopify, Slack and Replit; runs an in-house AI Lab supporting portfolio companies.

aka: Mila x Inovia Venture Scientist Fund

strategy.thesis: Early-stage fund created to commercialize frontier AI research from Canada's national AI institutes (Mila, Amii, Vector) and leading universities into AI-native companies, engaging at the earliest stages of company formation — often before a startup formally exists. Plans to invest in 55+ AI-native companies. Addresses that Canada has ~10% of top global AI talent but captures <2% of global AI VC.

summary.en: Early-stage AI venture fund launched January 2026 by Mila (Quebec AI Institute) and Inovia Capital, targeting US$100M (C$125M) to back 55+ AI-native companies spun out of Canada's national AI institutes (Mila, Amii, Vector) and top universities. Managed by Stéphane Marceau as a separate legal entity.

strategy.thesis: Backs enterprise-focused 'useful AI' startups in Québec — companies combining strong technical capability with domain expertise and defensible, vertical-specific business models, with go-to-market and proprietary client data as the moat. Plans ~30 investments.

summary.en: Québec-based pre-seed/seed AI fund launched September 2025, a spinoff of European firm Telegraph Hill Capital. Holds a $35M first close (targeting $40M) to back ~30 enterprise-focused 'useful AI' startups with $500K-$750K checks. Managed by Étienne Mérineau; backed by Investissement Québec, Teralys Capital and Inovia Capital.

summary.en: Toronto AI venture studio launched June 2025 by University of Toronto CS professors Daniel Wigdor and Tovi Grossman (with David and Ray Sharma). strategy.thesis: Founder and venture-development acceleration network for AI-enabled startups, operated by non-profit NEXT Canada, delivered in Toronto, Montreal and remotely.

investment.raw: No direct funding (program connects ventures to investors)

application_cycles: Applications opened Oct 16, 2025; deadline Dec 10, 2025; program runs Mar–Aug/Sep
program.eligibility: Canadian-incorporated, early-stage venture where AI is core; requires at least one business and one technical co-founder, each holding a minimum 10% equity; co-founders need Canadian citizenship/PR or valid work/study permit.

application.how_to_apply: Apply online via Airtable form linked from nextcanada.com/next-ai during annual cycle.

summary.en: AI-focused founder and venture-development accelerator run by non-profit NEXT Canada, delivered in Toronto, Montreal and remotely. Takes no equity and provides no direct funding, instead offering mentorship, education and investor access; the 2024 cohort had 100 founders across 45 ventures, and the program has helped launch 114+ AI startups.
